data.title: Aave Labs Seeks Approval for V4 Isolated Hub and Spoke for Custodied Collateral
data.description:
Aave Labs published an ARFC on September 14 seeking approval to deploy a new Aave V4 Isolated Hub and Spoke for institutional custodied collateral to be used as stablecoin borrowing collateral. According to ChainCatcher, institutional borrowers would keep collateral in custody at Anchorage during the loan term, while the custody balance would be represented onchain by the non-transferable custody collateral token CoCT, minted and burned by Chainlink-designed CustodySync.

Borrowers would stake CoCT on the Spoke and withdraw stablecoins from the Isolated Hub. The proposal says loan lifecycle events, including liquidation, would be synchronized between the custodian and Aave through Chainlink infrastructure. The scope is limited to one Isolated Hub and one Spoke governed by the Aave DAO, with no changes to existing Hubs, Spokes, or reserves.

The underlying assets would remain in custody at all times, with Anchorage holding the assets as the custodian and counterparty to the account control agreement, while Chainlink would not hold the assets. CoCT is described as a transfer-restricted ERC-20 that can only be used by the Hub, Spoke, and CustodySync, with minting and burning handled exclusively by CustodySync and each borrower position mapped to a separate contract.

The initial plan is to launch one CoCT backed by BTC held in Anchorage custody. The next step is discussion of the ARFC, followed by Snapshot if supported and then a final AIP submission with parameters.

data.title: AI Data Center Power Shortage Reshapes Gas Turbine and SOFC Supply Chains
data.description:
The power shortage created by the AI data center boom is reshaping global gas turbine and solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC) supply chains, with GE Vernova and Bloom Energy posting strong second-quarter order growth and revenue gains, according to Jiemian News. GE Vernova said second-quarter gas turbine new orders reached 12.1 GW, up 137% year on year, while its power segment backlog rose to $111.649 billion and the order book stretched to 5.31 years. Bloom Energy reported second-quarter revenue of $1.065 billion, up 165.5%, raised its full-year revenue guidance to $3.9 billion-$4.2 billion, and said it held about $20 billion in backlog.

Jiemian News said the overseas demand surge is filtering into China’s A-share market, but the supply chain is splitting into companies with real orders and those still trading on concepts. Jereh Group said it had won more than $3.1 billion in gas turbine generator set and related orders from November 2025 through the release of its half-year results, including a $1.465 billion supply contract signed in July by its J&F Power Systems unit with a major cloud services provider. The company also signed a strategic cooperation agreement with Siemens Energy in May. By contrast, companies such as Wanze Co., Yingliu Co., Sanhuan Group, and Zhenhua Co. are still largely in supplier qualification, sample delivery, or small-batch shipment stages, while some SOFC and gas turbine concept stocks have not disclosed formal orders from GE Vernova or Bloom Energy.

data.title: Ripple, Strategy Say CLARITY Act Defeat Does Not Change XRP, Bitcoin Status
data.description: Ripple and Strategy said the Senate’s 49-50 defeat of the CLARITY Act did not alter XRP or Bitcoin’s legal standing. According to BeInCrypto, Ripple chief legal officer Stuart Alderoty cited a 2023 federal ruling that XRP exchange sales were not securities and March SEC-CFTC guidance naming XRP a digital commodity. Strategy, formerly MicroStrategy, said Bitcoin has had U.S. legal and regulatory clarity for years and noted its 845,050 BTC stack was still about 1% above cost after the vote.

data.title: Blackstone CFO Says Firm’s Scale Gives It an Edge in the AI Boom
data.description:
Blackstone Chief Financial Officer Michael Chae said the firm’s portfolio construction and strategy allow it to capture growth in artificial intelligence, AI, and infrastructure, and to deploy and attract capital at scale. According to Sina Finance, Chae said at a Barclays conference on Tuesday that Blackstone completed nine initial public offerings for its portfolio companies over the past year, while six others have filed for listings around the world.

Chae said the alternative asset manager, which oversees $1.3 trillion in assets, invests in AI, power, life sciences, and private-market lending to companies. He said 70% of Blackstone’s largest investments over the past 12 months were concentrated in those areas and that it is now a good time to deploy capital.

He also said Blackstone raised more than $260 billion over the past year, its best 12-month period in nearly four years, and that institutional investor inflows jumped 50% over the same period. Chae said Blackstone’s AI investments will begin to show up in earnings as strong performance drives fee growth.

data.title: GEOPOLITICS | US Coast Guard Boards Texas-Bound Oil Tanker in Cyberattack Probe
data.description: US military forces and FBI agents boarded a Texas-bound oil tanker to investigate a cyberattack, and the Coast Guard confirmed the operation late Tuesday, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: Thai Finance Minister Keeps 2.5% Growth Forecast Despite Oil Price Surge
data.description: Thai Finance Minister Ekniti Nitithanprapas is sticking with the government’s forecast for 2.5% economic growth this year despite the surge in oil prices, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: Chile Central Bank Deputy Governor Sees Investment, Consumption Recovery
data.description: A senior Chilean central banker said investors should look beyond the economy’s recent slowdown and expect a recovery in investment and consumption, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: GEOPOLITICS | RBNZ Assistant Governor Karen Silk to Leave at Year-End
data.description:
Reserve Bank of New Zealand Assistant Governor Karen Silk will step down at the end of the year, according to Bloomberg.

The departure will trigger a refresh of the central bank’s senior leadership.

data.title: US Stocks Close: Tech Shares Under Pressure as AI Safety Debate Intensifies
data.description:
Micron rose 0.39% and ranked second in U.S. stock trading by value, with turnover of $34.948 billion. According to Sina Finance, Micron showed the world’s first 512GB DDR5 memory module, a 3DS RDIMM that uses through-silicon via stacking to maximize capacity in a single package. The company said the module supports 9,200MT/s transfer speeds, can deliver 12TB of memory in a single server under a dual-socket 24-slot configuration, and is expected to enter mass production in the second half of 2027. AMD and Intel are validating the module on next-generation server processor platforms.

Nvidia rose 0.57% and ranked fourth with turnover of $18.627 billion. According to Sina Finance, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said on Tuesday that no new laws or regulatory rules are needed for artificial intelligence safety, arguing that market forces will push companies to ensure safety while innovating. He made the remarks at a Salesforce event and said AI development does not have to choose between safety and speed.

Meta rose 0.70% and ranked fifth with turnover of $13.042 billion. According to Sina Finance, Meta Platforms plans to begin deploying its new in-house ARKE chip in data centers in the first half of next year. The company said it is testing the third-generation version of the series, code-named MTIA 450 or Arke, while the next version, code-named 500 or Astrid, is expected to finish design work in about a month and enter data-center use in 2027.

Tesla fell 0.67% and ranked sixth with turnover of $10.853 billion. According to Sina Finance, Elon Musk again hinted at the 2026 All-In Summit that SpaceX and Tesla could merge. The report said the two companies have already cooperated in several areas, including the Terafab semiconductor project.

Apple fell 0.52% and ranked ninth with turnover of $10.475 billion. According to Sina Finance, Apple pushed iOS 27 to users on Monday U.S. Eastern Time. The update’s main highlight is the public test phase for Siri AI, which Apple announced in June but had not yet formally delivered; it currently supports only English.

Amazon fell 2.02% and ranked 11th with turnover of $9.018 billion. According to Sina Finance, Amazon Web Services said some data centers in the Persian Gulf region still cannot restore data access after damage during the U.S.-Iran war. AWS said data stored only in its Bahrain data center and some network regions in the United Arab Emirates remains inaccessible.

AMD rose 2.19% and ranked 13th with turnover of $8.632 billion. Intel fell 0.05% and ranked 15th with turnover of $8.326 billion. According to Sina Finance, chipmaker Altera, backed by private equity giant Silver Lake and Intel, said on Tuesday that it has confidentially filed for an initial public offering with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, formally starting its return to the public market.

Dell rose 1.73% and ranked 20th with turnover of $5.417 billion. According to Sina Finance, Dell Technologies CEO Michael Dell said the AI boom will keep prices for computing equipment and personal computers rising, and that the structural shortage of hardware chips will likely worsen further in 2027. He said chip structural shortages are likely to be more severe in 2027 than in 2026 and that higher costs will be passed through to product pricing.

data.title: U.S. Military Says Iran Maritime Blockade Has Forced 103 Merchant Ships to Change Course
data.description: According to Sina Finance, the U.S. Central Command said it has continued carrying out maritime blockade operations against Iran. As of September 15, the command said the U.S. military had forced 103 merchant ships to change course.

data.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Expected at Xi Jinping State Dinner in Washington
data.description: According to CNBC, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is expected to attend a state dinner for Chinese leader Xi Jinping when Xi travels to Washington to meet with President Donald Trump next week. A person familiar with the matter said Huang's planned appearance is the latest sign of his alignment with Trump, and that relationship appeared stronger this week as the two pushed back against other tech CEOs who have warned about the risks of rapid AI advancement. AI is expected to be a main topic when Xi meets with Trump, and Huang was among a select group of CEOs who traveled to China with Trump earlier this year. It was not immediately clear who else has been invited to the dinner. A White House official said Trump invited several American business leaders to the dinner because he will prioritize making good deals for the country.

data.title: Copper Falls Near $6.30 As Supply Shortage And AI Demand Clash
data.description: Copper traded near $6.30 a pound on Tuesday, down almost 8% from its early August record after posting its first losing week since June. Economist Steve Hanke urged followers to stay long on copper six days ago, citing shrinking mine supply, according to BeInCrypto, while International Copper Study Group data showed global mine output fell 1.1% in the first half of 2026. Freeport-McMoRan’s Grasberg mine remains at roughly half capacity, Chile cut its forecast again, and AI data centers are adding demand.

data.title: AI | Trump Advisers Meet Anthropic Executive on Safety Risks
data.description:
Senior Trump administration officials met Tuesday with Anthropic PBC’s top Washington executive to discuss artificial intelligence safety risks, according to Bloomberg.

The meeting involved Trump advisers Howard Lutnick and Michael, Bloomberg reported.

data.title: Oaktree’s Poli Says Credit Investors Are Finally Being Paid to Take Risk
data.description: Credit investors are “being paid to take risk, finally,” Danielle Poli of Oaktree Capital Management said, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: AI TRENDS | Meta Plans Camera-Free Smart Glasses Launch This Fall
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, Meta plans to launch a pair of camera-free smart glasses this fall, with the internally codenamed Luna model featuring six microphones, voice interaction with Meta AI chatbot and the newly released consumer AI agent Muse, a side button to summon Meta AI, and open speakers that direct sound to the ear without blocking the ear canal.

data.title: AI TRENDS | OpenAI's Sam Altman Says AI Can Be Developed Safely
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said he believes AI companies can safely develop the technology without causing major harm to the public, and that he is very confident in his company’s and the industry’s ability to do so.

data.title: OpenAI Discusses New Private Funding Round at About $1.2 Trillion Valuation
data.description:
OpenAI is discussing a new private funding round with investors at a target valuation of about $1.2 trillion as it prepares for a future IPO. According to ChainCatcher, the company’s valuation reached $852 billion after a financing round completed in March this year.

The company is also discussing additional fundraising plans with large investors, and the talks are still at an early stage. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said an IPO may not come before 2027.

data.title: Blackstone Targets $8 Billion for Green Infrastructure Credit Fund
data.description: Blackstone Inc. is seeking to raise at least $8 billion for a private credit fund focused on renewables and digital infrastructure investments, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: STOCKS | U.S. Senate Republicans Weigh Fast-Track Bill to Curb Consumer Energy Costs
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, U.S. Senate Republicans are considering an accelerated legislative process to advance a bill before the November election aimed at curbing rising consumer energy costs, with the measure targeting energy-intensive data centers.
